examples.en: The new employee is being assigned to the sales team.
The desks are arranged by the window.
Police were stationed all over the place.

examples.ko: 다음 달부터 지방 지사로 배치될 거예요.
examples.en: I will be posted to a regional branch starting next month.

examples.ko: 가구가 잘 배치된 방은 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: A room with well-arranged furniture looks spacious.

examples.ko: 신입 사원은 여러 부서에 나뉘어 배치되고 있어요.
examples.en: The new hires are being split up and assigned to several departments.

explain: 사람은 '부서에 배치되다'처럼 일할 자리에 정해지고, 물건은 '가구가 배치되다'처럼 자리를 잡아요. 같은 뜻의 능동형은 '배치하다'이고, 회사에서는 '발령'이라는 말도 같이 써요. 보통 '~에 배치되다'로 장소나 부서가 꼭 따라와요.
explain_en: For people it means being assigned to a post, as in '부서에 배치되다'; for objects it means being set in a place, like furniture. The active form is 배치하다, and at companies 발령 is also used. It almost always comes with a place or department: '~에 배치되다'.

en: be compelled; be forced; be enforced

examples.en: There were many places where wearing a mask was mandatory.
This rule is imposed on all students.
Studying doesn't last long if it's forced.
I really hate forced overtime.
I exercise every day even when it isn't required.

examples.ko: 아무도 그 선택이 강제됐다고 생각하지 않아요.
examples.en: Nobody thinks that choice was forced.

explain: '강제되다'는 내 뜻과 상관없이 규칙이나 힘 때문에 어쩔 수 없이 하게 되는 상황에 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '억지로 하다', '어쩔 수 없이 하다'라고 더 많이 말하고, 이 단어는 규칙·제도·뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 반대로 스스로 하는 건 '자발적'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes being made to do something by rules or pressure, regardless of your will. In daily talk Koreans more often say '억지로 하다' or '어쩔 수 없이 하다'; 강제되다 appears more in rules, systems and news. The opposite is '자발적' (voluntary).

examples.en: Every student is given a number.
A lot of responsibility was given to this job.
Members will be granted a discount benefit.

examples.ko: 권한이 부여된 사람만 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who have been given permission can enter.

examples.ko: 새 계정에는 임시 비밀번호가 부여되고 있어요.
examples.en: Temporary passwords are being issued to new accounts.
A special mission was assigned to the player.

explain: '받다'보다 딱딱해서 공문, 규칙, 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 번호·권한·자격·책임·의미처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 주어지는 경우가 많아서, 선물이나 돈에는 '받다'를 써요. 주는 쪽은 '부여하다'예요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '받다' and shows up in official notices, rules and news. It is usually for intangible things such as numbers, authority, qualifications or meaning; for gifts or money Koreans use 받다. The giver's verb is 부여하다.

examples.en: At the meeting, people speak one by one in turn.
He raised his hand and spoke carefully.
May I speak too?
The CEO will speak in person today.

examples.ko: 누군가 발언할 때는 조용히 해 주세요.
examples.en: Please be quiet when someone is speaking.

examples.ko: 먼저 발언한 의견이 토론의 방향을 정했어요.
examples.en: The opinion stated first set the direction of the discussion.

explain: '말하다'와 달리 회의·토론·기자회견처럼 공식적인 자리에서 의견을 밝힐 때 써요. 친구와 수다를 떨 때는 쓰지 않아요. 명사 '발언'과 같이 '발언을 하다', '발언이 길다'로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike plain 말하다, it is for stating an opinion in formal settings such as meetings, debates and press conferences. You would not use it for chatting with friends. The noun 발언 is also common: '발언을 하다', '발언이 길다'.

examples.en: I volunteered to run the event.

examples.ko: 먼저 자원하는 사람이 없어서 제가 손을 들었어요.
examples.en: Nobody volunteered first, so I raised my hand.
The teacher gave points to the student who volunteered to clean.
Who wants to volunteer for tomorrow's presentation?
I was surprised because my younger brother offered to do the dishes.
He volunteers even for dangerous jobs.

explain: '자원하다'는 시키지 않았는데 스스로 나서서 맡겠다고 하는 거예요. 회의나 수업에서 하나를 맡을 때는 '내가 할게요', '지원할게요'라고 더 자주 말해요. 이 단어는 글이나 공식 자리에서 더 자연스러워요. '자원봉사'는 이 말이 들어간 다른 단어예요.
explain_en: It means stepping forward on your own to take something on without being told. In class or meetings people more often say '내가 할게요' or '지원할게요'. 자원하다 sounds more natural in writing and formal settings. '자원봉사' (volunteer work) is a separate word that contains it.

examples.ko: 여러 재료를 조합해서 새 요리를 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a new dish by combining several ingredients.

examples.ko: 색을 잘 조합하면 옷이 더 예뻐 보여요.
examples.en: If you combine colors well, the outfit looks prettier.

examples.ko: 숫자 네 개를 조합해 비밀번호를 만들어요.
examples.en: I make a password by combining four numbers.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 사진과 글을 조합할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This app lets you combine photos and text.

examples.ko: 단어를 조합해 문장을 만드는 연습을 했어요.
examples.en: We practiced making sentences by combining words.

examples.ko: 서로 다른 방법을 조합한 결과가 좋았어요.
examples.en: The result of combining different methods was good.

explain: '섞다'는 눈에 보이는 것을 그냥 섞는 느낌이고, '조합하다'는 정해진 요소들을 맞춰서 새것을 만드는 느낌이에요. 색, 숫자, 재료, 방법처럼 요소가 따로 있을 때 어울려요. 명사 '조합'은 '좋은 조합'처럼 어울리는 짝을 말할 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: While 섞다 just means to mix, 조합하다 means putting set elements together to make something new, such as colors, numbers, ingredients or methods. The noun 조합 is also used for a good pairing, as in '좋은 조합'.

examples.en: That theory was proven by an experiment.

examples.ko: 그의 말이 거짓이 아니라는 것이 증명돼요.
examples.en: It is proven that his words are not false.
Skill is proven by results.
It is a medicine whose effect has not yet been proven.

examples.ko: 이 사진으로 제 말이 증명될 거예요.
examples.en: This photo will prove what I said.
It's a well-proven method, so you can trust it.

explain: '증명되다'는 어떤 사실이 근거나 결과로 확실해졌다는 뜻이고, 수학·과학·재판·뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 주어가 사람이면 '증명하다', 사실이나 이론이면 '증명되다'를 써요. 비슷한 '확인되다'는 있는지 없는지를 알게 된 것이고, '증명되다'는 옳다는 것을 보여 준 거예요.
explain_en: It means a fact has been made certain by evidence or results, common in math, science, trials and news. With a person doing it use 증명하다; with the fact or theory as subject use 증명되다. 확인되다 means you found out whether something is so, while 증명되다 means it was shown to be correct.

examples.ko: 피부를 햇빛에 너무 오래 노출하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't expose your skin to sunlight for too long.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 고객 정보를 실수로 노출했어요.
examples.en: That company accidentally exposed customer information.

examples.ko: 피부를 많이 노출하는 옷은 겨울에 추워요.
examples.en: Clothes that show a lot of skin are cold in winter.
You must not expose a child to danger.

examples.ko: 자신의 생각을 잘 노출하지 않는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He's a person who doesn't reveal his thoughts easily.
We plan to show the ad to more people.

explain: '보여 주다'보다 딱딱하고, 숨기는 게 좋은 것이나 위험한 것을 밖에 드러낸다는 느낌이 있어요. 햇빛·위험·정보·광고와 자주 같이 써요. 비슷한 '드러내다'는 감정이나 생각에 더 자연스러워요. 스스로 드러나면 '노출되다'예요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than 보여 주다 and often means leaving something that should be hidden or protected open to the outside. It pairs with sunlight, danger, information and ads. 드러내다 is more natural for feelings and thoughts. When it happens passively, use 노출되다.

examples.en: I went for a walk to change my mood.
The company switched its direction to online sales.

examples.ko: 화면을 가로로 전환하면 더 넓게 보여요.
examples.en: If you switch the screen to landscape, it looks wider.
Please don't suddenly change the subject.
We will switch the class to online.

examples.ko: 다른 일로 전환한 뒤에 훨씬 행복해졌어요.
examples.en: I became much happier after switching to a different job.

explain: '바꾸다'는 아무 물건이나 상황에 쓰지만, '전환하다'는 방향·방식·상태를 크게 바꿔서 다른 쪽으로 돌린다는 느낌이에요. '기분 전환', '방향 전환', '온라인으로 전환'처럼 굳은 짝이 많아요. 옷이나 물건을 바꿀 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Where 바꾸다 works for almost anything, 전환하다 means turning direction, method or state to a different side in a big way. It has many set pairs: 기분 전환, 방향 전환, 온라인으로 전환. You would not use it for swapping clothes or objects.

examples.en: The Wi-Fi suddenly won't connect.
You get a notification when you are connected to the server.
I liked that the site connected right away.
It's hard to get connected now because there are many users.
I got connected to the meeting, but there's no sound.
Please check the devices that are connected.

explain: 사람이 하는 행동은 '접속하다', 연결이 되었거나 안 된 상태는 '접속되다'라고 해요. 그래서 '접속이 안 돼요', '접속이 안 되네요'처럼 인터넷이 안 될 때 아주 자주 들어요. '연결되다'는 전화나 사람 사이에도 쓰지만 '접속되다'는 주로 인터넷·서버에 써요.
explain_en: What a person does is 접속하다; the state of being connected or failing to connect is 접속되다. You hear '접속이 안 돼요' all the time when the internet fails. 연결되다 also covers phones and relationships, but 접속되다 is mostly for the internet and servers.

examples.en: This shop carries imported snacks.
Please don't treat me like a child.

examples.ko: 깨지기 쉬운 물건이니까 조심해서 취급해 주세요.
examples.en: It breaks easily, so please handle it with care.
They treated it as a special case.
Our company deals in used cars.
It's a place that treats every customer the same.

explain: 가게가 어떤 물건을 파는지 말할 때는 '취급하다'가 '팔다'보다 직업적이고 자연스러워요. 사람을 '~처럼 취급하다'로 대하는 태도를 말할 때는 대부분 기분이 나쁜 상황이에요. 물건을 다룰 때는 '취급 주의'라는 표시를 자주 봐요.
explain_en: For what a shop sells, 취급하다 sounds more professional than 팔다. '~처럼 취급하다' is about how someone is treated and is mostly used when you feel disrespected. On parcels you often see the label '취급 주의' (handle with care).

examples.en: The video was edited nicely.
The interview is edited to fit the length.

examples.ko: 사진이 너무 많이 편집된 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think the photo has been edited too much.

examples.ko: 이 책은 여러 사람의 글이 모여 편집되었어요.
examples.en: This book was compiled from the writings of several people.
Unnecessary parts are cut out and the broadcast comes out.
When the file is edited, it is saved automatically.

explain: 영상·사진·글·책을 다듬고 정리해서 하나로 만든다는 뜻이에요. 글을 고치는 '수정하다'보다 전체 구성과 순서를 손보는 느낌이 강해요. 하는 사람은 '편집하다', 일을 하는 사람은 '편집자'예요.
explain_en: It covers tidying and arranging video, photos, text or books into one finished piece. Compared with 수정하다 (fix), it feels more about the overall structure and order. The doer's verb is 편집하다 and the professional is a 편집자 (editor).

examples.en: That movie opens next week.
I haven't opened the gift box yet.
Please drink opened milk quickly.
It was released last year but is still popular.
If you open the packaging, you can't get a refund.
The video of opening the new album is popular.

explain: 영화가 처음 극장에 걸릴 때, 그리고 포장·봉투를 처음 뜯을 때 둘 다 써요. 영화는 '개봉하다'지만 책이나 노래는 '출간하다', '발매하다'라고 해요. 이미 뜯은 물건은 '개봉한 제품', 안 뜯은 것은 '미개봉'이에요.
explain_en: It covers both a movie first showing in theaters and breaking the seal on packaging. Movies are 개봉하다, but books and music use 출간하다 and 발매하다. An already opened product is '개봉한 제품', and an unopened one is '미개봉'.

examples.ko: 저 건물은 백 년 전에 건축됐어요.
examples.en: That building was built a hundred years ago.
A new library will be built here.
A hanok is a house built from wood.
It's a bridge built long ago, so it isn't sturdy.
A building is under construction, so it's noisy.

examples.ko: 그 성당은 오 년에 걸쳐 건축되었어요.
examples.en: That cathedral was built over five years.

explain: 집·성·다리 같은 큰 건물을 짓는 것에는 '건축하다'를, 일상 말에서는 '짓다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. 그래서 '집을 건축했어요'보다 '집을 지었어요'가 자연스러워요. '건축되다'는 건물의 역사나 설명글에 더 잘 나와요. 도로나 다리 공사는 '건설되다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: For big structures like houses, castles and bridges, 건축하다 is the formal verb, but daily speech uses 짓다 far more: '집을 지었어요' sounds more natural than '집을 건축했어요'. 건축되다 shows up in explanations of a building's history. For roads and bridges, 건설되다 is also common.

examples.ko: 이 사전은 오만 개의 단어를 수록해요.
examples.en: This dictionary includes fifty thousand words.
We included ten songs on the new album.

examples.ko: 이 잡지는 신인 작가의 시를 수록한 특별호를 냈어요.
examples.en: This magazine put out a special issue that includes poems by new writers.

examples.ko: 작가는 이 책에 여행기를 수록하려고 해요.
examples.en: The author is trying to include travel essays in this book.
If you include many photos, the book price goes up.
The editor decided to include the full interview.

explain: 책·사전·앨범·잡지 같은 곳에 글이나 곡을 실을 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '들어 있다', '실려 있다'가 더 자연스럽고 '수록하다'는 소개글이나 설명에 많이 나와요. 안에 실린 쪽은 '수록되다'예요.
explain_en: Used when putting writing or songs into a book, dictionary, album or magazine. In daily talk '들어 있다' or '실려 있다' is more natural; 수록하다 appears in blurbs and descriptions. The passive is 수록되다.

examples.en: The new product announcement is getting attention in the industry.
That player's growth is drawing attention.
The upcoming result is getting a lot of attention.
There is a reason the new technology is drawing attention.
The small shop suddenly started drawing attention.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 신인 중에서 가장 주목되는 사람이에요.
examples.en: That singer is the one drawing the most attention among newcomers.

explain: 사람들의 눈길이 그쪽으로 모인다는 뜻이고, 뉴스와 글에서 '주목되다'로 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '주목받다'가 더 흔하고, 비슷한 '관심을 끌다'는 부드러운 말이에요. '주목하세요'처럼 사람에게 '여기를 보세요'라고 할 때는 '주목하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means everyone's eyes are turning to it, common in news and articles. In daily speech 주목받다 is more usual, and 관심을 끌다 is softer. To tell people 'look here' you use the active 주목하다, as in '주목하세요'.

examples.en: A seat has been prepared for the guests.

examples.ko: 행사장에 쉴 수 있는 공간이 마련돼 있어요.
examples.en: There is a resting area set up at the venue.
The moving money was finally put together.
A new measure will be worked out soon.
It's a program arranged for the students.

examples.ko: 집을 사려면 돈이 먼저 마련되어야 해요.
examples.en: To buy a house, the money has to be ready first.

explain: '준비되다'와 비슷하지만 '마련되다'는 자리·돈·방법·제도처럼 앞으로 쓸 것을 갖춰 놓았다는 느낌이에요. 능동은 '마련하다'로 '집을 마련하다', '대책을 마련하다'처럼 자주 써요. 음식이나 짐처럼 바로 쓸 것에는 '준비되다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Like 준비되다, but 마련되다 suggests having set up something for future use, such as a seat, money, a method or a system. The active 마련하다 appears in '집을 마련하다' and '대책을 마련하다'. For food or luggage ready to use, 준비되다 is more natural.

examples.en: A player was injured in the soccer game.
Many people ended up injured in the accident.
If you run too hard, you can get injured.

examples.ko: 부상당한 선수는 이번 경기에 못 나가요.
examples.en: The injured player can't play in this game.

examples.ko: 그는 부상당하지 않으려고 준비 운동을 해요.
examples.en: He warms up so as not to get injured.
Fortunately no one was hurt.

explain: '다치다'는 일상에서 가장 흔하고, '부상당하다'는 사고·전쟁·운동 경기처럼 뉴스에 나오는 상황에 더 어울려요. 친구가 넘어져서 다쳤으면 '다쳤어요'라고 해요. 명사 '부상'은 '부상을 입다', '부상 선수'로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: 다치다 is the everyday word; 부상당하다 fits news-type situations such as accidents, war and sports. If a friend fell and got hurt, say '다쳤어요'. The noun 부상 is also common: '부상을 입다', '부상 선수'.

examples.en: The two people's personalities contrast with each other.

examples.ko: 밝은 색과 어두운 색이 크게 대비되는 그림이에요.
examples.en: It's a painting where bright and dark colors contrast strongly.
The result was a contrast with last year's.

examples.ko: 하얀 옷이 검은 배경과 잘 대비돼서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The white clothes contrast well with the black background, so they stand out.
The older and younger brothers contrasted, starting from their height.

examples.ko: 좋은 점과 나쁜 점이 대비되게 정리했어요.
examples.en: I organized the good and bad points so they contrast.

explain: 두 가지를 나란히 놓았을 때 차이가 뚜렷하게 보인다는 뜻이에요. '비교되다'는 어느 쪽이 나은지 견주는 느낌이 있고, '대비되다'는 차이가 서로 반대처럼 선명한 느낌이에요. '대비하다'는 '준비하다'라는 전혀 다른 뜻이니 구분하세요.
explain_en: It means a difference stands out clearly when two things are set side by side. 비교되다 leans toward judging which is better, while 대비되다 stresses a sharp, almost opposite difference. Be careful: 대비하다 is a different word meaning to prepare for something.

examples.en: The construction wraps up this week.
The meeting wrapped up faster than I thought.
If the work wraps up well, let's have a meal together.
This year's project will be finished in December.
I'm relieved the event ended safely.
I still have homework that isn't finished.

explain: '끝나다'는 일이 단순히 끝난 거고, '마무리되다'는 끝을 잘 정리해서 완성되었다는 느낌이에요. 마지막 단계에서 쓰는 말이라 시작한 지 얼마 안 된 일에는 어울리지 않아요. 능동은 '마무리하다'로 '일을 마무리하다', '이야기를 마무리하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 끝나다 just means something ended; 마무리되다 means it was wrapped up neatly and completed. It is a last-stage word and sounds odd for something just started. The active 마무리하다 is used in '일을 마무리하다' and '이야기를 마무리하다'.

en: putting something on the market; releasing

examples.ko: 새 앨범 발매가 다음 달로 미뤄졌어요.
examples.en: The new album's release was pushed to next month.
The line got long after news of the game console's release.
Everything sold out on the first day of sale.

examples.ko: 이 가수의 발매 기념 팬 행사가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a fan event for this singer's release.
Expectations were high even before release.

examples.ko: 한정판은 발매 후 며칠 안에 구해야 해요.
examples.en: The limited edition has to be bought within a few days of release.

explain: 음반·게임·상품이 처음 가게에 나와 팔리기 시작하는 것을 말해요. 책은 '출간', 영화는 '개봉', 앱이나 서비스는 '출시'라고 해서 대상에 따라 다른 단어를 써요. 앨범과 게임기에는 '발매'가 가장 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means a record, game or product first appears in stores and goes on sale. Korean picks different words by object: 출간 for books, 개봉 for movies, 출시 for apps and services. 발매 fits albums and game consoles best.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 다음 주에 새 앨범을 발매해요.
examples.en: That singer is releasing a new album next week.

examples.ko: 회사가 새 게임을 올해 안에 발매하려고 해요.
examples.en: The company wants to release a new game within this year.
The song released last year is still popular.
Fans eagerly counted the days until it was released.
They released the limited edition first.
I hope they release the regular edition next year too.

explain: 주어는 가수·회사처럼 상품을 내놓는 쪽이에요. 앨범과 게임, 한정판처럼 가게에서 파는 물건에 어울리고, 앱은 '출시하다', 책은 '출간하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 팬이 앨범을 사는 건 '발매하다'가 아니라 '사다'예요.
explain_en: The subject is the one putting a product out, such as a singer or company. It suits albums, games and limited editions sold in stores; apps are 출시하다 and books 출간하다. A fan buying an album is simply 사다, not 발매하다.

examples.en: This factory manufactures car parts.
The company makes and sells food itself.
I learned how to manufacture soap.
That's a company that makes cosmetics.
The product made last year is past its expiration date.
To manufacture safely, you need facilities.

explain: '만들다'는 아무 때나 쓰는 말이고, '제조하다'는 공장에서 재료로 물건을 만드는 산업적인 말이에요. 집에서 요리하거나 만들기를 할 때는 쓰지 않아요. '제조업', '제조일자'처럼 합쳐서도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 만들다 is the all-purpose word; 제조하다 is the industrial one for making goods from materials in a factory. You would not use it for home cooking or crafts. It often appears in compounds like 제조업 (manufacturing industry) and 제조일자 (date of manufacture).

examples.ko: 이 방법은 이미 여러 번 검증됐어요.
examples.en: This method has already been verified many times.
We only sell products whose safety has been verified.
That rumor hasn't been verified yet.

examples.ko: 실력이 검증되면 정식 직원이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Once your skills are verified, you can become a regular employee.
A new theory is verified through experiments.
Let's wait until the effect is verified.

explain: 사실인지 맞는지를 확인하는 과정을 거쳐서 믿을 만하다고 인정받은 상태를 말해요. '증명되다'는 옳다는 것이 확실히 보인 결과이고, '검증되다'는 확인 절차를 통과한 거예요. 광고나 리뷰에서 '검증된 제품'이라는 말을 자주 봐요.
explain_en: It describes something that passed a process of checking whether it is true or correct and is accepted as reliable. 증명되다 is the result of being shown to be right; 검증되다 means it passed verification. You often see '검증된 제품' in ads and reviews.

examples.en: Electricity is supplied to every house.
The water was cut off and wasn't supplied.
Fresh vegetables are supplied to the shop every day.

examples.ko: 부품이 제때 공급되면 공장이 계속 돌아가요.
examples.en: If parts are supplied on time, the factory keeps running.
Here there are drinks supplied for free.
The amount supplied fell short, so the price went up.

explain: 전기·물·가스처럼 생활에 필요한 것이 필요한 곳으로 들어오는 상황에 자주 써요. 주는 쪽은 '공급하다'이고, 받는 쪽 입장에서는 '공급받다'예요. 경제에서는 '수요'와 짝이 되어 '수요와 공급'으로 나와요.
explain_en: It is common for utilities like electricity, water and gas reaching where they are needed. The giver's verb is 공급하다 and the receiver's is 공급받다. In economics it pairs with 수요 as '수요와 공급' (supply and demand).

examples.en: We made a plan, so let's carry it out now.
When you run the program, the screen turns on.
Don't just think about it; do it right away.
The team leader put the new policy into effect.
Start by setting a goal you can actually carry out.
I wrote the result of what I carried out in the report.

explain: '하다'보다 딱딱하고, 세운 계획이나 결정을 실제로 해 본다는 느낌이에요. 컴퓨터에서는 프로그램을 '실행하다'가 아주 자주 쓰여서 '실행 파일', '실행 버튼'을 볼 수 있어요. 비슷한 '실천하다'는 다짐이나 약속을 몸으로 옮길 때 어울려요.
explain_en: Stiffer than 하다, it means actually carrying out a plan or decision. On computers 실행하다 is very common for running programs: you will see 실행 파일 and 실행 버튼. 실천하다 is similar but fits turning a resolution or promise into action.

examples.en: This Buddha statue was carved from stone.
I bought a box with flowers carved on the wood.
A dragon is carved above the door.
The ice is being carved into a lovely shape.
That name is carved on the gravestone.

examples.ko: 벽에 조각될 그림이 아직 안 정해졌어요.
examples.en: The picture to be carved on the wall hasn't been decided yet.

explain: 돌·나무·얼음 같은 재료를 깎아서 모양을 만든 상태를 말해요. '새기다'는 글자나 무늬를 파는 느낌이고, '조각되다'는 입체적인 모양이 만들어진 느낌이에요. 명사 '조각'은 '조각상', '조각가'로도 자주 써요. 같은 소리의 '조각'(한 조각 케이크의 조각)은 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes shaping stone, wood or ice by carving. 새기다 is more about cutting letters or patterns, while 조각되다 suggests a three-dimensional form. The noun 조각 appears in 조각상 and 조각가. Note the same-sounding 조각, as in a piece of cake, is a different word.

en: be replaced; be substituted; be changed

examples.en: The old computer was replaced with a new one.
Two players are substituted in the second half.

examples.ko: 고장 난 부품은 곧 교체될 거예요.
examples.en: The broken part will be replaced soon.

examples.ko: 감독이 교체된 뒤 팀 분위기가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: After the coach was replaced, the team's mood changed.
The filter has to be replaced every month.
The old sign is being replaced.

explain: '바뀌다'보다 부품, 사람, 선수처럼 같은 자리에 있던 것을 다른 것으로 갈아 끼운다는 느낌이에요. 새것으로 바꾸는 상황에 쓰고, 단순히 달라지는 것에는 '바뀌다'를 써요. 능동은 '교체하다'로 '배터리를 교체하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Compared with 바뀌다, it means swapping what sat in a spot, like a part, person or player, for another. Use it for replacement with something new; for simply becoming different, use 바뀌다. The active 교체하다 appears in '배터리를 교체하다'.

examples.en: They are repairing the old bridge.

examples.ko: 낡은 지붕을 보수해야 비가 안 새요.
examples.en: You have to repair the old roof to stop the leaks.
The city repaired the road.

examples.ko: 한옥을 보수하는 일은 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Repairing a hanok takes a long time.
There isn't enough money to repair the building.

examples.ko: 보수한 곳이 다시 무너질까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried the repaired part will collapse again.

explain: 건물·다리·도로처럼 큰 시설의 낡거나 상한 곳을 고칠 때 써요. 작은 물건이나 기계에는 '고치다'나 '수리하다'를 써요. 소리가 같은 '보수'는 급여나 정치 성향을 뜻하기도 해서 문장 속에서 구분해야 해요.
explain_en: It is for fixing worn or damaged parts of large structures such as buildings, bridges and roads. For small items or machines use 고치다 or 수리하다. The sound 보수 also means pay or a conservative leaning, so tell them apart from context.

examples.en: The new system will be set up within this year.

examples.ko: 서로 믿는 관계가 구축되기까지 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time before a relationship of trust is built.
A Wi-Fi network was set up at the school.
Once the data is built up, searching gets easy.
We inspected the facilities that had been set up.
A secure security system is being built.

explain: 눈에 보이는 건물보다 시스템·네트워크·관계·데이터처럼 틀을 차근차근 쌓아서 만든다는 뜻이에요. 건물을 짓는 일에는 '건설되다', '짓다'를 써요. 뉴스와 회사 문서에서 자주 나오고, 능동은 '구축하다'예요.
explain_en: Rather than physical buildings, it fits frameworks built up step by step: systems, networks, relationships and data. For buildings use 건설되다 or 짓다. It is frequent in news and company documents; the active is 구축하다.

examples.en: My grandmother's life was truly hard and unlucky.
He's a person born to an unfortunate fate.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 주인공의 인생이 너무 기구해요.
examples.en: The drama's main character's life is so unlucky.
I heard the story of a life lived with great misfortune.
I didn't know my fate would be this unfortunate.
His life was so unfortunate that it hurt my heart.

explain: 하루 일이 안 풀린 정도가 아니라, 인생이나 운명이 계속 힘들고 순탄하지 않을 때 써요. '불행하다'보다 문학적이고 이야기에 어울려요. 주로 '기구한 운명', '기구한 삶', '기구한 인생'처럼 짝으로 나와요.
explain_en: It is not for a bad day but for a life or fate that keeps being hard and bumpy. It is more literary than 불행하다 and fits stories. It mostly appears in set pairs: 기구한 운명, 기구한 삶, 기구한 인생.

examples.en: Prices are rising, but my salary keeps stagnating.
My grades keep stalling, so I'm worried.
The population has been stagnant for ten years.
The company's growth has stalled for several years.

examples.ko: 정체하는 시기에는 쉬면서 방법을 바꿔 보세요.
examples.en: During a stagnant period, rest and try changing your approach.

examples.ko: 정체한 느낌이 들 때는 새로운 일을 해 봐요.
examples.en: When you feel stuck, try something new.

explain: 길이 막힐 때는 '막히다'가 일상에서 훨씬 자연스러워요. '정체하다'는 성장이나 성적이 더 나아가지 못하고 멈춰 있을 때 써요. 교통 뉴스에서는 '정체되다'나 명사 '정체'(정체 구간)를 더 자주 써요. 같은 소리의 '정체'(정체를 밝히다처럼 진짜 모습)는 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: For roads, '막히다' is far more natural in daily talk. '정체하다' is for growth or grades that stall and stop improving. Traffic news more often uses '정체되다' or the noun '정체' (as in 정체 구간). The same-sounding '정체', meaning true identity, as in '정체를 밝히다', is a different word.
